title: Technology Sector Update for 07/02/2018: VMW,DVMT,GOOG,MTLS,VMW, GOOGL, DVMT,GOOG,MTLS,NEPNEP
text:

Tech stocks were trimming some of their prior declines, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 Monday losing less than 0.3% although the Philadelphia semiconductor index still was posting a nearly 0.7% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ VMware ( VMW ) has climbed more than 10% on Monday after Dell Technologies ( DVMT ) said it will buy out VMWare's tracking stock for $21.7 billion in cash and stock, with investors getting the choice of receiving 1.3665 of a new VMWare Class C share or $109 in cash - up to a total of $9 billion - for each Class V share they now own. The Class C stock will be listed on the New York Stock Exchange after the deal closes. Dell issued the Class V tracking shares after Dell completing its merger with EMC and holds an 81% economic stake in the software firm and almost all of its voting stock.
In other sector news:
- Materialise NV ( MTLS ) slid as much as 2% on Monday after the company late Friday disclosed plans to raise up to $250 million through a mixed shelf registration that includes ordinary shares, American Depository Shares, preference shares and warrants, according to a regulatory filing by the software firm late Friday.
- NextEra Energy Partners LP ( NEP ) was almost 2% lower Monday afternoon, recovering somewhat from a nearly 3% decline in mid-morning trading, although the company said it completed the sale of its Canadian renewable energy assets to affiliates of Cordelio Power for CND740 million, or about $563 million. The transaction included NextEra's former interests in four wind generation plants and two solar energy facilities, all located in Ontario, having a combined generating capacity of 396 megawatts. Cordelio also assumed CND889 million, or about $676 million, of existing NextEra debt,
- Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) was edging lower Monday, paring a nearly 2% retreat that followed reports the technology comglomerate has invested in an electric scooter startup as part of a larger $300 million funding round that already included its Google Ventures affiliate. Google Ventures is said to be leading the funding rounds in Lime, but the Financial Times report did not specify how much Alphabet is investing in the funding round, although sources told the newspapert it matched Google Ventures' amount.
